question.text: Under the IFSCA general rule, how often must a Regulated Entity update CDD information for different risk categories of customers?

answer.text: Annually for high-risk customers, once every three years for medium-risk customers, and once every five years for low-risk customers
Every year for all customers regardless of risk category
Only when the customer specifically requests a review of their records
Only at the time of account opening and never again during the relationship

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the IFSCA workbook (pp.106-107), the general periodicity of CDD updates is risk-based: annually for high-risk customers, once every three years for medium-risk, and once every five years for low-risk customers. (A separate two/eight/ten-year schedule applies narrowly to resident Indian customers with an existing client relationship with the Financial Group in India.) The Trap: "Every year for all customers" is too frequent and ignores risk differentiation. "Only when the customer requests it" or "only at account opening" both abandon the mandatory periodic-review obligation entirely. Where the Financial Group's risk categorisation differs from the RE's, the stricter periodicity applies. Note: Document the CDD-update policy clearly and set automated reminders aligned to the risk category — missing periodic KYC reviews is a common compliance finding in audits.
